## Eduard (Eddie) Bukin

All slides on this site were written and taught by **Eduard (Eddie) Bukin**, an
applied economist and open-source data scientist working on impact evaluation,
land markets and geospatial analysis. He taught the quantitative part of
MK-068-EN at the **Institute of Agricultural Policy and Market Research**,
Justus Liebig University Giessen, in the winter semesters 2023/24 and 2024/25.

## About the course

**MK-068-EN (TM) Empirical Research Methods** is a module of the Faculty of
Agricultural Sciences, Nutritional Sciences and Environmental Management (FB09)
at JLU Giessen. The materials here are its quantitative part, *Statistics and
Econometrics*: seven weeks that go from populations and samples, through
descriptive statistics, distributions and correlation, to hypothesis testing,
confidence intervals and linear regression, with worked examples from
development economics and agricultural research. It was taught as Part 2 of the
module in 2023/24 and as Part 1 in 2024/25.

Both cohorts have their own page: [Winter Semester 2024/25](cohorts/ws-2024-25.qmd)
and [Winter Semester 2023/24](cohorts/ws-2023-24.qmd).

## Reusing these materials

The materials are published openly so that students can revisit them after the
course and so that other instructors can build on them. The
[repository](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/) contains every
source file: the `.qmd` decks and the parts they include, the R setup scripts,
the cleaned datasets with the scripts that produced them, and the PDFs shared
with each cohort.

If you reuse or adapt them, please credit **Eduard Bukin** and link back to
[ebukin.github.io](https://ebukin.github.io). The datasets carry their own
acknowledgement requirements; see the [datasets](data.qmd) page.

## Colophon

Built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/). Slides are
[revealjs](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/) decks written in
Quarto markdown with R code chunks; their executed results are frozen in the
repository so that the site rebuilds without re-running the analysis. The site
is deployed automatically from the
[GitHub repository](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/) and follows
the structure of the author's
[MP223 Applied Econometrics](https://ebukin.github.io/mp223-2022-aem-R-public/)
course site.
